$USB Deposit costs are the hinge in the entire bank argument this quarter. 
 
A bank earns net interest income, the gap between what it charges borrowers and pays savers. Early in a rate cycle that gap widens, because loan rates move up faster than the rate on a checking account. 
 
Later it narrows. Savers stop accepting almost nothing and start shopping. Where any bank sits on that curve is the single most useful number in its filing, and it is why one bank's net interest income came in slightly under forecast this week while two others cleared theirs. 
 
Full explainer, plain English: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hlan3N9D9mU
